_readme: Hand-curated join between sample repos and documented product nodes.
Product node ids come from data/products.json (derived from llms.txt).
A repo with no entry here is reported as 'undocumented' — a sample with no
matching doc page. That is a real finding, not an error. Never add a bogus
_scoreableSectionsNote: Only these sections count toward the coverage percentage. Getting Started,
Integration Options, API References and Resources are reference material —
a runnable sample is not the right artifact for 'Country Codes' or
'Versioning'. They are still rendered in the UI, marked as not scoreable,
_excludeNodesNote: Prefix match against product node ids. These are documented products that this
team does not own the samples for: in-store terminal integrations belong to the
terminal SDK stack, and Plugins / direct API are cart-plugin and reference
territory. Excluding them keeps the gap list a buildable backlog rather than a
list of other teams' work. They still render in the UI, marked out of scope.
_coverageTargetNote: How many in-scope products should have a runnable sample. Set a number here and
the dashboard draws a target line across the strip and reports the shortfall.
Left null until the team commits to one, because an invented target is worse
than no target: it grades the work against a number nobody agreed to.
_coverageBandsNote: Grades the headline percentage so a reader never has to guess whether the
number is good. Bands are inclusive upper bounds, checked in order.
_languageColumnsNote: The four majors. Python and Go folders are still recorded per repo and shown
in the detail panel, but they are not columns and never affect the score.
